method: candidate lines proposed by corridor detection; identity decided from printed address runs and street-name labels
why_not_one_block_off: Both sheets print the corridor's name in it: sheet 68's right margin reads 'AVE. H OR BALL' with neighbour sheet number 69 beside it, and sheet 69's left margin reads 'AVE. H OR BALL' with neighbour sheet number 68 beside it. Sheet 68's other labelled avenue is 'AVE. G OR WINNIE' and sheet 69's is 'AVE. I OR SEALY', matching the keymaps (68: E-H, 69: H-K). The cross-street runs place the hundred-block change on this corridor: sheet 68's block 334, between Winnie and Ball, prints '701 703 705 707 709 711 / 713 715 717 719 721 723' and '702 704 706 708 710 712 / 714 716 718 720 722 724'; sheet 69's block 274, between Ball and Sealy, prints '801 803 805 807 809 811 / 813 815 817 819 821 823' and '802 804 806 808 810 812 / 814 816 818 820 822 824'. The avenue frontages face even-to-odd across it: sheet 68's east column reads 3402,3404,...,3428 and sheet 69's west column reads 3401,3403,...,3427. Detection's candidates (2778 / 698) both fall inside blocks; centres read off the green native rulers with half-widths taken from the fully drawn Avenue G and Avenue I.
